Give the honest reason, not a gesture: the natural block-triangular induction on $n$ loses one unit of the range at each step and therefore proves nothing new, and the boundary case $k=n-t$ is equivalent to the nonsingularity of the disjointness matrix, whose known proofs go through eigenvalues of the Johnson scheme or Gottlieb's construction. Neither is among this page's declared prerequisites. Say "not built here", never that the library does not develop it, and do not state the unproved theorem as though the page had it.

items.title: Monomials, coefficients, degree in each variable and total degree in $F[x_1,\dots,x_n]$
items.strategy: Using the iterated construction of [[def-multivariate-polynomial-ring-by-iteration]], prove that every $f\in F[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ has a unique expansion $f=\sum_{\mathbf{t}}c_{\mathbf{t}}x^{\mathbf{t}}$ over finitely many multi-indices $\mathbf{t}\in\mathbb{N}^{n}$, where $x^{\mathbf{t}}=x_1^{t_1}\cdots x_n^{t_n}$; define $[x^{\mathbf{t}}]f=c_{\mathbf{t}}$, the **degree in $x_i$** as the largest $t_i$ with $c_{\mathbf{t}}\ne0$, and the **total degree** as the largest $t_1+\cdots+t_n$ with $c_{\mathbf{t}}\ne0$, with the zero polynomial handled separately. THE LIBRARY BUILDS THE MULTIVARIATE RING BY ITERATION AND STOPS THERE, so this expansion is an obligation of this page, proved by induction on $n$ from the univariate coefficient expansion. Also define evaluation at a point of $F^{n}$ by iterating [[thm-universal-property-of-a-polynomial-ring]].

items.title: If $\deg_{x_i}P<\lvert S_i\rvert$ for each $i$ and $P$ vanishes on $S_1\times\cdots\times S_n$, then $P=0$
items.strategy: Induction on $n$. Base $n=1$: a nonzero univariate polynomial of degree $d$ has at most $d$ roots ([[thm-root-bound-for-polynomials-over-a-domain]]), and $d<\lvert S_1\rvert$ roots are supplied, so $P=0$. Step: write $P=\sum_{j\le d}P_j(x_1,\dots,x_{n-1})x_n^{j}$ with $d=\deg_{x_n}P<\lvert S_n\rvert$; for each fixed point of $S_1\times\cdots\times S_{n-1}$ the resulting univariate polynomial in $x_n$ vanishes on $S_n$, hence is zero, hence every $P_j$ vanishes on $S_1\times\cdots\times S_{n-1}$; apply the inductive hypothesis to each $P_j$. Statement is Alon Lemma 2.1. THE HYPOTHESIS IS STRICT INEQUALITY, and the companion page's counterexample is the equality case. Landmark.

items.title: Reducing $f$ modulo $g_i(x_i)=\prod_{s\in S_i}(x_i-s)$ lowers each $\deg_{x_i}$ below $\lvert S_i\rvert$, preserves the values on the grid, and does not change the coefficient of a monomial of top total degree
items.strategy: Replace, repeatedly, an occurrence of $x_i^{\lvert S_i\rvert}$ by $x_i^{\lvert S_i\rvert}-g_i(x_i)$, which has $\deg_{x_i}<\lvert S_i\rvert$; formally, subtract multiples $h_ig_i$ with $\deg h_i\le\deg f-\deg g_i$ and induct on the total degree. Prove three separate claims: the reduction $\tilde f$ has $\deg_{x_i}\tilde f<\lvert S_i\rvert$; $\tilde f$ and $f$ agree at every point of $S_1\times\cdots\times S_n$ because each $g_i$ vanishes there; and if $\deg f=\sum_it_i$ then $[x^{\mathbf{t}}]\tilde f=[x^{\mathbf{t}}]f$, because every subtracted term $h_ig_i$ has total degree at most $\deg f$ and its monomials of that top degree are divisible by $x_i^{\lvert S_i\rvert}$, so with $t_i<\lvert S_i\rvert$ they cannot contribute to $x^{\mathbf{t}}$. THE THIRD CLAIM IS THE ONE THAT DOES THE WORK and it is where a proof is usually waved through.

items.title: Alon's Combinatorial Nullstellensatz: if $\deg f=\sum_it_i$, the coefficient of $x_1^{t_1}\cdots x_n^{t_n}$ in $f$ is nonzero, and $\lvert S_i\rvert>t_i$, then $f(s_1,\dots,s_n)\ne0$ for some $s_i\in S_i$
items.strategy: Suppose $f$ vanishes on the whole grid. Reduce it by [[lem-grid-reduction-of-a-multivariate-polynomial]] to $\tilde f$ with $\deg_{x_i}\tilde f<\lvert S_i\rvert$; $\tilde f$ still vanishes on the grid, so $\tilde f=0$ by [[thm-polynomial-identity-lemma]]. But the third clause of the reduction lemma says $[x^{\mathbf{t}}]\tilde f=[x^{\mathbf{t}}]f\ne0$, a contradiction. Statement is Alon Theorem 1.2, quoted with all three hypotheses; the hypothesis that the coefficient of the TOP monomial is nonzero is load-bearing and the companion page carries the false statement that drops it. Landmark.

items.title: If $p$ is prime and $0\le k\le m<p$ then $p\nmid\binom{m}{k}$
items.strategy: Use the $p$-adic valuation: $\binom{m}{k}k!(m-k)!=m!$ in $\mathbb{N}$ by [[thm-binomial-closed-formula]], and $v_p(m!)=0$ because none of $1,\dots,m$ is divisible by $p$ when $m<p$ ([[lem-p-adic-valuation-basic]], [[lem-p-adic-valuation-additive]]). Additivity of $v_p$ then forces $v_p\binom{m}{k}=0$. Cauchy–Davenport needs exactly this and it is a numbered step there, not an observation.

items.title: Cauchy–Davenport: for $p$ prime and nonempty $A,B\subseteq\mathbb{Z}/p$, $\lvert A+B\rvert\ge\min\{p,\lvert A\rvert+\lvert B\rvert-1\}$
items.strategy: If $\lvert A\rvert+\lvert B\rvert-1>p$ the bound is $p$ and $A+B=\mathbb{Z}/p$ by a pigeonhole argument on $a+b=c$; give that case its own steps. Otherwise suppose $\lvert A+B\rvert\le\lvert A\rvert+\lvert B\rvert-2$, choose $C\supseteq A+B$ with $\lvert C\rvert=\lvert A\rvert+\lvert B\rvert-2$, and set $f(x,y)=\prod_{c\in C}(x+y-c)$ over the field $\mathbb{Z}/p$ ([[thm-z-mod-p-is-a-field]]). Its total degree is $\lvert C\rvert=t_1+t_2$ with $t_1=\lvert A\rvert-1$, $t_2=\lvert B\rvert-1$, and the coefficient of $x^{t_1}y^{t_2}$ is $\binom{\lvert A\rvert+\lvert B\rvert-2}{\lvert A\rvert-1}$, nonzero in $\mathbb{Z}/p$ by [[lem-a-binomial-coefficient-with-top-below-a-prime-is-nonzero-modulo-that-prime]] since $\lvert A\rvert+\lvert B\rvert-2<p$. Apply [[thm-combinatorial-nullstellensatz]] with $S_1=A$, $S_2=B$ to get $a\in A$, $b\in B$ with $f(a,b)\ne0$, contradicting $a+b\in A+B\subseteq C$. Statement is Alon Theorem 3.2. PRIMALITY IS LOAD-BEARING and the companion page's counterexample is a composite modulus. Landmark.

items.title: Covering $\{0,1\}^{n}$ minus the origin by affine hyperplanes avoiding the origin needs at least $n$ of them
items.strategy:
Let $H_1,\dots,H_m$ be given by $\langle a_k,xangle=b_k$ with $b_k
e0$, covering every vertex of $\{0,1\}^n$ except the origin and missing the origin. Suppose $m<n$ and consider $f(x)=(-1)^{n+m}\,b_1\cdots b_m\prod_{i}(x_i-1)\;-\;\prod_{k} igl(\langle a_k,xangle-b_k igr)$ over $\mathbb{R}$. Show $f$ vanishes on all of $\{0,1\}^{n}$: at the origin the two terms cancel by the choice of constant, and at every other vertex both terms vanish. Then $\deg f=n$ with the coefficient of $x_1\cdots x_n$ equal to $\pm b_1\cdots b_m
e0$ (the second product has degree $m<n$ and cannot contribute), so [[thm-combinatorial-nullstellensatz]] with $S_i=\{0,1\}$ gives a vertex where $f
e0$ — a contradiction. VERIFY THE SIGN AND THE CONSTANT BY EVALUATING AT THE ORIGIN as a numbered step; this is the only place a slip can hide. Statement is Alon Theorem 6.3 (Alon–Füredi). Landmark.

items.title: Multilinear polynomials and the reduction $x_i^{2}\mapsto x_i$ on the cube
items.strategy: A polynomial in $F[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ is **multilinear** when $\deg_{x_i}\le1$ for every $i$; equivalently it is an $F$-combination of the monomials $x_T=\prod_{i\in T}x_i$ for $T\subseteq[n]$. Define the **multilinear reduction** $\widetilde{f}$ by repeatedly replacing $x_i^{2}$ by $x_i$, i.e. by reducing modulo the polynomials $x_i^{2}-x_i$ in the sense of [[lem-grid-reduction-of-a-multivariate-polynomial]] with $S_i=\{0,1\}$. Record that $\deg\widetilde f\le\deg f$ and that $x_T$ has total degree $\lvert T\rvert$.

items.title: $\widetilde f$ is multilinear, agrees with $f$ at every point of $\{0,1\}^{n}$, has no larger total degree, and is the unique multilinear polynomial with that agreement
items.strategy: Existence and agreement are [[lem-grid-reduction-of-a-multivariate-polynomial]] with $S_i=\{0,1\}$ (note $t^2=t$ for $t\in\{0,1\}$, so the reduction changes no value there). Uniqueness: a multilinear polynomial vanishing on $\{0,1\}^n$ is zero by [[thm-polynomial-identity-lemma]] with $\lvert S_i\rvert=2>1\ge\deg_{x_i}$. The degree clause needs its own step: reduction never raises total degree.

items.title: The functions $\{0,1\}^{n}\to F$ obtained from $x_T$ with $\lvert T\rvert\le s$ are linearly independent, so they span a space of dimension $\sum_{i=0}^{s}\binom{n}{i}$
items.strategy: A vanishing combination is a multilinear polynomial vanishing on the cube, hence the zero polynomial by [[lem-every-polynomial-agrees-on-the-cube-with-its-multilinear-reduction]], hence has all coefficients zero by the uniqueness of the monomial expansion in [[def-monomials-multidegree-and-total-degree]]. The count of index sets is $\sum_{i\le s}\binom{n}{i}$ by [[def-binomial-coefficient]] and [[thm-sum-rule]]. Boundary $s=0$ and $s=n$ are stated.

items.title: $L$-intersecting families
items.strategy: For a finite set $L\subseteq\mathbb{N}$, a family $\mathcal{F}$ of subsets of $[n]$ is **$L$-intersecting** when $\lvert A\cap B\rvert\in L$ for all distinct $A,B\in\mathcal{F}$. Note that nothing is required of $\lvert A\rvert$ itself — that is the difference from the uniform hypotheses used earlier on the page, and it is exactly what makes the ordering trick in the next theorem necessary. Record that Oddtown and Fisher are the cases $L=\{$even sizes$\}$ (not of this form) and $L=\{t\}$ respectively; state that comparison precisely or not at all.

items.title: An $L$-intersecting family on $[n]$ with $\lvert L\rvert=s$ has at most $\sum_{i=0}^{s}\binom{n}{i}$ members
items.strategy: Order $\mathcal{F}=\{F_1,\dots,F_m\}$ with $\lvert F_1\rvert\le\cdots\le\lvert F_m\rvert$. For each $i$ put $f_i(x)=\prod_{\ell\in L,\ \ell<\lvert F_i\rvert}\bigl(\langle x,v_{F_i}\rangle-\ell\bigr)$ over $\mathbb{R}$, of total degree at most $s$. Then $f_i(v_{F_i})=\prod_{\ell<\lvert F_i\rvert}(\lvert F_i\rvert-\ell)\ne0$, and for $j<i$, $f_i(v_{F_j})=0$: indeed $\lvert F_i\cap F_j\rvert\in L$ and $\lvert F_i\cap F_j\rvert\le\lvert F_j\rvert\le\lvert F_i\rvert$, with equality forcing $F_i\subseteq F_j$ and then $F_i=F_j$, so the intersection size is a member of $L$ strictly below $\lvert F_i\rvert$ and appears in the product. THE STRICT-INEQUALITY TRUNCATION OF THE PRODUCT IS WHAT REMOVES THE USUAL EXTRA HYPOTHESIS; make it a numbered step. Apply [[lem-triangular-independence-criterion]] to the multilinear reductions $\widetilde{f_i}$ paired against evaluation at $v_{F_j}$, then count dimensions with [[lem-the-multilinear-monomials-of-bounded-degree-are-independent-on-the-cube]]. Statement is Babai–Frankl's nonuniform Ray-Chaudhuri–Wilson bound. Landmark.

items.title: If $\mathcal{F}$ does not shatter $T$ then $x_T$ agrees on $\{v_F:F\in\mathcal{F}\}$ with a combination of the $x_S$ for $S\subsetneq T$
items.strategy: Choose $A\subseteq T$ realised by no member of $\mathcal{F}$ as $F\cap T$, and set $g(x)=\prod_{i\in A}x_i\prod_{i\in T\setminus A}(1-x_i)$. At $x=v_F$ the value is $1$ when $F\cap T=A$ and $0$ otherwise, so $g$ vanishes on every $v_F$. Expanding, $g=(-1)^{\lvert T\setminus A\rvert}x_T+\sum_{A\subseteq S\subsetneq T}(\pm1)x_S$, which rearranges to the claim. Each of the three facts — the value of $g$ at a cube point, the expansion, and the rearrangement — is its own step.

items.title: A second proof of Sauer–Shelah, from the multilinear polynomial space
items.strategy: Let $\mathcal{F}$ have VC dimension at most $d$ and let $V$ be the space of all functions $\mathcal{F}\to\mathbb{R}$, of dimension $\lvert\mathcal{F}\rvert$. Every such function is the restriction of a multilinear polynomial by [[lem-every-polynomial-agrees-on-the-cube-with-its-multilinear-reduction]] (interpolate on the cube and reduce). By [[lem-an-unshattered-set-reduces-a-monomial-on-a-family]] and induction on $\lvert T\rvert$, the restriction of $x_T$ for $\lvert T\rvert>d$ lies in the span of the restrictions of $x_S$ with $\lvert S\rvert<\lvert T\rvert$; hence the restrictions of the $x_T$ with $\lvert T\rvert\le d$ span $V$, and $\lvert\mathcal{F}\rvert=\dim V\le\sum_{i\le d}\binom{n}{i}$. A GENUINELY DIFFERENT ROUTE from the shifting proof: a spanning argument in a polynomial space replaces a compression argument, and neither proof is a rearrangement of the other. State the agreement with [[thm-sauer-shelah]] explicitly.

items.title: The shifting proof of Sauer–Shelah uses no field and no vector space
items.strategy: Say precisely which of this page's machinery the shifting proof does and does not use: no incidence vector, no field, no bilinear form and no dimension — only injections, a strictly decreasing natural number and a count of subsets. A reader arriving from Oddtown and Fisher will otherwise assume the theorem inherits a field hypothesis it does not have. Contrast with [[thm-sauer-shelah-by-multilinear-polynomials]], which does use the page's machinery, so the contrast is concrete rather than asserted. Required by the page's design.

items.title: Which field each bound is proved over, and what changes when it is replaced
items.strategy: One short paragraph per theorem, naming the field and the property of it that the proof spends: Oddtown over $\mathbb{F}_2$ using only bilinearity and the diagonal; Eventown over $\mathbb{F}_2$ using the dimension of an orthogonal complement; Fisher over $\mathbb{R}$ using that a sum of squares vanishes only when every term does; Graham–Pollak over $\mathbb{R}$ for the same reason; the Nullstellensatz over an arbitrary field; Cauchy–Davenport over $\mathbb{Z}/p$ with primality used to make it a field and to keep a binomial coefficient invertible. Then say what the companion page's false statements test. A JUSTIFYING REMARK: it explains hypotheses and names only items on this page. Do not count anything and do not rank the results.

title: Linear Algebra Methods in Combinatorics — Examples

items.title: An Oddtown family of four clubs on four citizens, and why a fifth cannot be added
items.strategy: Take the four singletons on $[4]$, check both parities, and then check by hand that no fifth subset of $[4]$ can be adjoined: a candidate must have odd size and meet each singleton evenly, which forces it to be disjoint from every point. Also display the incidence matrix over $\mathbb{F}_2$ and verify $NN^{\mathsf{T}}=I_4$. This makes both [[thm-oddtown]] and [[cor-the-oddtown-bound-is-attained]] concrete.

items.title: The pairing construction gives an Eventown family of size $2^{\lfloor n/2\rfloor}$
items.strategy: Group the points of $[n]$ into the pairs $\{0,1\},\{2,3\},\dots$, leaving one point unpaired when $n$ is odd, and take every union of pairs. Check both parity conditions and count $2^{\lfloor n/2\rfloor}$ sets. Write $n=4$ out in full — $\varnothing$, $\{0,1\}$, $\{2,3\}$, $\{0,1,2,3\}$, four sets, matching $2^{2}$ — and then $n=5$, where the same four sets are still maximal and $2^{\lfloor 5/2\rfloor}=4$, so the floor is visible rather than asserted. Check the result against [[thm-eventown]] and [[thm-every-maximal-eventown-family-is-maximum]].

items.title: The seven lines of the Fano plane meet pairwise in one point, and Fisher's bound is tight
items.strategy: Write the seven three-element subsets of $[7]$ explicitly (for instance the translates of $\{0,1,3\}$ modulo $7$), verify that every two of them meet in exactly one point by listing the twenty-one pairs or by a short modular argument, and check $m=7\le n=7$ against [[cor-uniform-fisher-inequality]]. Present the Fano plane as a SET SYSTEM only: block designs and projective planes are not among the page's prerequisites, and no design-theoretic vocabulary is used.

items.title: $K_4$ decomposed into three complete bipartite graphs, and no decomposition into two
items.strategy: Give the star decomposition $(\{0\},\{1,2,3\})$, $(\{1\},\{2,3\})$, $(\{2\},\{3\})$ and check every edge is covered exactly once. Then check the lower bound directly at $m=2$ by running the argument of [[thm-graham-pollak]] on the explicit two-equation system, exhibiting a nonzero solution and the resulting contradiction.

items.title: All subsets of $[4]$ of size at most $2$: VC dimension $2$ and exactly $\sum_{i\le2}\binom{4}{i}=11$ members
items.strategy: List the eleven sets, verify that $\{0,1\}$ is shattered, verify that no three-element set is shattered (the full triple is missing from every trace), and compare with the bound $1+4+6=11$ of [[thm-sauer-shelah]]. Then run one down-shift on a family that is not downward closed and check both compression lemmas on it.

items.title: $W_{1,2}(4)$ written out, and its rank computed
items.strategy: Display the $4\times6$ matrix with rows the points of $[4]$ and columns the six pairs, row reduce it over $\mathbb{Q}$, and confirm the rank is $4$ as [[thm-rank-of-the-point-inclusion-matrix]] predicts. Also check the composition identity $W_{0,1}(4)W_{1,2}(4)=2\,W_{0,2}(4)$ by direct multiplication.

items.title: $A=B=\{0,1,2\}$ in $\mathbb{Z}/7$: the sumset has five elements and the bound is tight
items.strategy: Compute $A+B=\{0,1,2,3,4\}$, so $\lvert A+B\rvert=5=\lvert A\rvert+\lvert B\rvert-1$, matching [[thm-cauchy-davenport]] exactly. Then take $A=\{0,1,2,3\}$, $B=\{0,1,2,3,4\}$ and check the other branch, where the bound is $7$ and the sumset is everything.

items.title: Applying the Nullstellensatz by hand to $f(x,y)=x^{2}y+xy^{2}+x+y$ over $\mathbb{Q}$
items.strategy: Identify $\deg f=3$, the multi-index $(t_1,t_2)=(2,1)$ and the coefficient $1\ne0$; take $S_1$ with three elements and $S_2$ with two and exhibit a point where $f\ne0$, as [[thm-combinatorial-nullstellensatz]] guarantees. Then run [[lem-grid-reduction-of-a-multivariate-polynomial]] on the same $f$ for those grids and check the three claims of that lemma on the reduction. Verify every displayed coefficient before shipping.

items.title: The six $2$-subsets of $[4]$ are $\{0,1\}$-intersecting, and the bound $\sum_{i\le2}\binom{4}{i}=11$ holds
items.strategy: Check that any two distinct pairs meet in zero or one point, so $L=\{0,1\}$ and $s=2$; compare $6\le11$ from [[thm-frankl-wilson-nonuniform-bound]]. Then build the polynomials $f_i$ of that theorem for this family, multilinearise two of them by hand, and verify the triangular pattern of values that the proof uses.

items.title: The $n$ hyperplanes $x_i=1$ cover $\{0,1\}^{n}$ except the origin, so the Alon–Füredi bound is tight
items.strategy: Check that a nonzero vertex has some coordinate equal to $1$ and that the origin lies on none of the hyperplanes, so $n$ hyperplanes suffice; with [[thm-alon-furedi-hyperplane-cover-of-the-cube]] this makes $n$ exact. Then do $n=2$ in full, listing the four vertices and the two lines.

items.title: FALSE: an Oddtown family on $[n]$ has at most $n-1$ members
items.strategy: Refute with the $n$ singletons of [[cor-the-oddtown-bound-is-attained]], written out for $n=4$ and in general. The Refutation should also say where the plausible improvement would have to come from — a strict inequality in the dimension count — and why [[lem-a-family-with-independent-incidence-vectors-has-at-most-n-members]] gives no such thing.

items.title: FALSE: distinct nonempty $A_1,\dots,A_m\subseteq[n]$ whose pairwise intersections all have the same parity satisfy $m\le n$
items.strategy: THE PAGE’S PEDAGOGICAL PAYLOAD, and it must be stated as a PROPOSITION about set systems, not as a claim about a proof. The false statement is the $\mathbb{F}_2$ shadow of [[thm-nonuniform-fisher-inequality]]: over $\mathbb{R}$ the hypothesis is $\lvert A_i\cap A_j\rvert=t$ for all $i\ne j$, and over $\mathbb{F}_2$ all that survives of it is that the intersection sizes share a parity, since [[lem-the-standard-form-of-two-incidence-vectors-is-the-intersection-size]] sees an intersection only through $\lvert A_i\cap A_j\rvert\bmod 2$. Refute with an Eventown family from [[ex-an-eventown-family-of-maximum-size]]: every pairwise intersection is even, so all of them share a parity, and there are $2^{\lfloor n/2\rfloor}$ sets by [[thm-eventown]], which exceeds $n$ from $n=6$ on; drop $\varnothing$ if the nonemptiness clause is wanted and the count is still $2^{\lfloor n/2\rfloor}-1$. Exhibit the family in full for a concrete $n$ and check the two conditions on it. Then name the exact step of [[lem-real-vectors-with-equal-pairwise-products-and-larger-norms-are-independent]] that has no $\mathbb{F}_2$ analogue: the expansion ends in $\sum_ic_i^2(d_i-t)+t(\sum_ic_i)^2=0$ and concludes that each term vanishes, which uses that a sum of nonnegative reals vanishes only when every summand does. $\mathbb{F}_2$ carries no order, so there is nothing to run that step on — and the further clause $\langle v_i,v_i\rangle>t$ has no $\mathbb{F}_2$ analogue at all, which is exactly what the Eventown family exploits.

items.title: FALSE: a family on $[n]$ of VC dimension at most $d$ has at most $n^{d}$ members
items.strategy: CHECK THE WITNESS BEFORE SHIPPING. The true bound is $\sum_{i\le d}\binom{n}{i}$, which exceeds $n^{d}$ for small $n$: at $n=1$, $d=1$ the family $\{\varnothing,\{0\}\}$ has VC dimension $1$ and two members while $n^{d}=1$; verify this instance completely, and give one more, checking the VC dimension of each family by listing its traces. Then state the correct polynomial bound of [[cor-sauer-shelah-polynomial-bound]] and say exactly which inequality the false claim over-tightens.

items.title: FALSE: $\langle x,y\rangle=\sum_ix_iy_i$ makes $\mathbb{F}_2^{n}$ an inner product space
items.strategy: State the claim in the form a reader might write it and refute against [[def-inner-product-space]]: an inner product requires $\langle x,x\rangle$ to be a nonnegative real and to vanish only at $0$, and $\mathbb{F}_2$ carries no order at all. Exhibit $x=(1,1)$ with $\langle x,x\rangle=0$ and $x\ne0$. Then say what IS true: the form is a nondegenerate symmetric bilinear form, and every use of it on the page needs only bilinearity, so nothing is lost.

items.title: FALSE: if $\deg f=\sum_it_i$ and $\lvert S_i\rvert>t_i$ then $f$ is nonzero somewhere on $S_1\times\cdots\times S_n$
items.strategy: The dropped hypothesis is that the coefficient of $x_1^{t_1}\cdots x_n^{t_n}$ is nonzero. Refute with $f(x,y)=x^{2}-x$ over $\mathbb{Q}$, $t_1=t_2=1$, $S_1=S_2=\{0,1\}$: the total degree is $2=t_1+t_2$, each $\lvert S_i\rvert=2>1$, and yet $f$ vanishes at all four grid points, because the coefficient of $xy$ is $0$. Display the four evaluations. Then cite [[thm-combinatorial-nullstellensatz]] for the correct statement and note that the identity lemma does not apply either, since $\deg_x f=2$ is not below $\lvert S_1\rvert$.

items.title: A set family whose incidence vectors are dependent over $\mathbb{F}_2$ and independent over $\mathbb{R}$
items.strategy: Take $A_1=\{0,1\}$, $A_2=\{1,2\}$, $A_3=\{0,2\}$ in $[3]$, with incidence vectors $(1,1,0)$, $(0,1,1)$, $(1,0,1)$. Over $\mathbb{F}_2$ the three sum to $0$, so they are dependent; over $\mathbb{R}$ the incidence matrix has determinant $2\ne0$, so they are independent. Compute both, showing the determinant expansion. THE ITEM IS ABOUT THE FIELD BEING A HYPOTHESIS, which is why the page states one on every theorem.

items.title: In $\mathbb{Z}/4$ the sets $A=B=\{0,2\}$ have $\lvert A+B\rvert=2$, below the Cauchy–Davenport bound $3$
items.strategy: Compute $A+B=\{0,2\}$ — the four sums $0+0$, $0+2$, $2+0$, $2+2$ give $0,2,2,0$ — so $\lvert A+B\rvert=2<3=\min\{4,\lvert A\rvert+\lvert B\rvert-1\}$. DISPLAY ALL FOUR SUMS: the sumset is $\{0,2\}$ and not $\{0\}$, and a witness whose arithmetic is not shown is where this item would go wrong. Then say exactly which step of [[thm-cauchy-davenport]] fails: $\mathbb{Z}/4$ is not a field, so the polynomial argument has no domain to work in, and $\{0,2\}$ is a proper subgroup, which is the general obstruction — a subgroup $A=B=H$ always has $A+B=H$, so the deficit is as large as the subgroup allows. Cite [[thm-z-mod-p-is-a-field]] for the primality that is being spent.

items.title: $P(x)=x(x-1)$ vanishes on $\{0,1\}$ although $\deg_x P=\lvert\{0,1\}\rvert$
items.strategy: The one-variable instance shows the inequality in [[thm-polynomial-identity-lemma]] must be strict. Give also a two-variable instance, $P(x,y)=x(x-1)$ on $\{0,1\}\times\{0,1\}$, and check that the hypothesis fails only in the first variable. Say which numbered step of the identity lemma consumes the strictness.
